title: Semiabelian homomorphisms killing invertible torsion are divisible
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A semiabelian $k$-group algebraic space means a smooth separated finite-type commutative group object $G$ in algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] admitting an exact sequence $0\to T\to G\to A\to0$ of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site], where $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^t$ for some integer $t\geq0$ and $A/k$ is an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Here $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, group-object operations induce functorial group operations on $U$-points, and exactness means that $T$ is the kernel and sections of $A$ locally lift to $G$ for fppf coverings. Smoothness and finite type are tested on etale scheme charts, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $G,H$ be two such spaces and let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Write $[n]_G:G\to G$ for the sum of $n$ copies of $\operatorname{id}_G$, and $G[n](k)=\{x\in G(k):[n]_Gx=0\}$. If a homomorphism $f:G\to H$ of $k$-group algebraic spaces satisfies $f(x)=0$ for every $x\in G[n](k)$, there is a unique homomorphism $b:G\to H$ of $k$-group algebraic spaces with $f=b\circ[n]_G$. Equivalently $f=n b$ in the group of homomorphisms, where $n b$ is pointwise addition of $n$ copies of $b$.

source.place: Proposition 5.21, pp.103–104 (quotient universal property), and §5(e), pp.108–111 (quotient by a homomorphism kernel); §8.21, p.152 (multiplication on the abelian quotient), and Theorem 12.9, pp.233–234 (multiplication on a split torus). Semiabelian application: multiplication by invertible n is a finite etale surjective homomorphism, so killing its geometric kernel is exactly the quotient-factorization condition. Group-space representability over a field is recalled in Deligne §1.1(a), p.131.

external.place: I Remarks 8.11(f) and 8.12, printed p.39, for the abelian special case

proof.text: Put $p=[n]_G$. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-invertible-multiplication] to the semiabelian group $G$ and the given invertible integer $n$. In particular the scheme-test fibre $K=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{e,G,p}G$ is a finite etale scheme over $k$. Its functor of points is exactly $K(U)=\{x\in G(U):p(x)=0\}$, by the fibre-product definition.

source.place: Proposition 5.21, printed p.104, quotient factorization; agent sheaf-theoretic version for algebraic spaces

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to the scheme map $K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and its unique base point. Its fibre is $K$ itself, and it is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$. Because $k$ is algebraically closed, each such extension is $k$. Thus the inclusions indexed by $K(k)=G[n](k)$ form an open cover of $K$. On each inclusion $\operatorname{Spec}k\to K$, the maps $f|_K$ and zero agree by hypothesis. By the sheaf property of the algebraic space $H$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], they agree on this cover, hence on $K$. Equivalently, for every scheme $U$ and every $z\in K(U)$ one has $f_U(z)=0$.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2); algebraic spaces as fppf sheaves: spaces.tex Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space)

proof.text: For every $k$-scheme $U$ and $y\in G(U)$, [lem-sfb-semiabelian-invertible-multiplication] gives a scheme cover $q:V=U\times_{y,G,p}G\to U$ with its tautological lift $x\in G(V)$ satisfying $p(x)=y|_V$. The map $q$ is finite etale surjective, hence an fppf cover by [def-pc-fppf-site] and [def-weil-etale-morphism], which makes etale maps flat and locally of finite presentation. On $V\times_U V$ its two lifts $x_1,x_2$ have $p(x_1-x_2)=0$. Step 2 gives $f(x_1)-f(x_2)=f(x_1-x_2)=0$. Since $H$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], $f(x)$ glues uniquely to a section $b_U(y)\in H(U)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.21, printed p.104, quotient factorization; agent sheaf-theoretic version for algebraic spaces

proof.text: Any two local lifts of the same $y$ differ by a section of $K$ on their common pullback cover, so step 2 and sheaf uniqueness show that the glued value is independent of the lifts. For $a:W\to U$, restricting the cover and lift of step 3 gives $b_U(y)|_{W}=b_{W}(y|_{W})$. The maps $b_U$ are therefore a natural transformation $G\to H$, hence a morphism of algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. If $y=p(z)$ for $z\in G(U)$, the global lift $z$ gives $b_U(p(z))=f_U(z)$. Thus $b\circ p=f$.

source.place: Proposition 5.21, printed p.104, quotient factorization; agent sheaf-theoretic version for algebraic spaces

proof.text: For $y,y'\in G(U)$ choose local lifts $x,x'$ on the common refinement of their covers from step 3. Then $x+x'$ lifts $y+y'$ and $f(x+x')=f(x)+f(x')$. The independence just proved and sheaf uniqueness give $b_U(y+y')=b_U(y)+b_U(y')$. The zero lift gives $b_U(0)=0$, so $b$ is a group homomorphism. If $c\circ p=f$, then on any such lift $c_U(y)|_V=c_V(p(x))=f_V(x)=b_U(y)|_V$, hence $c_U(y)=b_U(y)$. This proves uniqueness. Finally $b_U([n]x)=n b_U(x)$ on every scheme $U$; therefore $b\circ[n]_G=n b$, and the stated equivalence follows.

Step 1 uses the new node with U=Spec k and y=e, so the kernel K is a finite etale k-scheme. Step 2 applies lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points: K is a disjoint union of copies of Spec k indexed by G[n](k), and fppf-sheaf uniqueness in H (def-trf-algebraic-space) gives f|_K=0 on every test scheme, which is the 'for all R' condition of Milne Prop 5.21 (p.104, checked). Step 3 uses the finite etale surjective cover, which is fppf by def-weil-etale-morphism and def-pc-fppf-site, and glues with p(x1-x2)=0. Steps 4-5 (independence of lifts, naturality, b∘p=f, additivity, uniqueness, f=nb) are genuinely elementary. New node: true (split torus power map with n invertible, Stacks 0BFH/03RP for the abelian part, torsor factorization). It is statement-only, self-contained, cites definitions that define what they are cited for, and does not restate the item (no f, no H). Small cases checked: n=1, G=G_m (n|r), and the characteristic-p counterexample when n is not invertible.
